root_cause: Output current on channel C1 exceeded the configured threshold, tripping the protection on the MC4x.
fix_steps: Step 1: Inspect wiring and connector on output C1 for shorts or chafing.
Step 2: Measure load resistance; confirm it is within the actuator spec.
Step 3: Verify the current limit in IQANdesign matches the actuator rating.
notes: Specific to firmware 6.x. In 7.x the default threshold changed.

root_cause: The CAN controller entered bus-off after exceeding the transmit error counter, usually from termination or baud-rate mismatch.
fix_steps: Step 1: Confirm 120 ohm termination at both physical ends of the bus.
Step 2: Check that every node shares the same baud rate.
Step 3: Inspect CAN_H/CAN_L for opens or shorts to supply/ground.
notes: Intermittent bus-off often points to marginal termination rather than wiring faults.

root_cause: Supply voltage dropped below the brown-out threshold during a high-load transient.
fix_steps: Step 1: Measure battery voltage under load; confirm it stays above 9V.
Step 2: Check ground and supply harness for voltage drop.
Step 3: Verify alternator output and battery health.
notes: Most common on cold-start with weak batteries.
